chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn Al-Hakam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'There is no desertion (ceasing of relationship) for more than three (days).'

key_terms.ثَلَاث: Three (days), indicating the maximum limit for the period of desertion.
key_terms.هِجْرَة: Desertion or severing of ties/relationship, specifically referring to a temporary cooling-off period or estrangement.

ai.seo_question: What is the maximum duration for severing ties or desertion between Muslims according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In Shia jurisprudence, this hadith from Al-Kafi defines the maximum duration for 'hijrah' (temporary estrangement) between individuals, preventing minor disputes from escalating into prolonged feuds. Scholars interpret this limit as a safeguard for social cohesion, emphasizing that silence or separation should not exceed three days to encourage timely reconciliation and maintain the bonds of brotherhood.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father and Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin Shazaan, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hisham Bin Al Hakam, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘There should be no desertion (ceasing of relationship) for more than three (days)’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father and Muhammad ibn Isma’il from Fadl ibn Shadhan from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hisham ibn al-Hakam from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “
The Messenger of Allah has said, ‘(Due to) walking out on another person (separation) should not continue more than three days.’”
